features.name: mechanical polish
features.description: Look for spelling, grammar, salutation accuracy, and other execution errors; this captures how much care and professionalism the letter signals through its surface quality.

levels.descriptor: Frequent obvious errors or salutation mistakes distract from the content and materially undermine confidence.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains understandable and broadly professional.
Only minor occasional slips appear, with generally polished presentation.
The letter is clean or nearly clean, with no distracting mistakes and strong attention to detail.

features.evidence: The moment that shaped my engineering priorities
features.name: opening distinctiveness
features.description: Look for whether the opening gives a vivid role-relevant premise or falls back on generic application language; this captures how memorable and purposeful the letter feels from the start.

levels.descriptor: The letter opens generically, such as simply stating an application or interest.
The opening is competent and relevant, but conventional.
The opening is memorable through a belief, problem framing, or career through-line tied to the role.
The opening is especially vivid and role-specific, immediately setting up a compelling case for fit.

features.evidence: too many signals, too few experts
features.name: security scaling insight
features.description: Look for whether the applicant identifies the job as a systems problem of scaling scarce security expertise through automation; this captures understanding of the role's core leverage.

levels.descriptor: Shows generic interest in security or Google without articulating the underlying problem.
Mentions automation or reduced manual work, but only at a broad level.
Clearly frames the work as scaling vulnerability handling or security response through tooling.
Shows nuanced insight into leverage points such as triage, signal overload, variant analysis, or lifecycle embedding.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: platform orientation
features.description: Look for explicit preference for foundational or central tooling whose gains propagate across teams; this captures fit for a core internal platform role.

levels.descriptor: Focuses mostly on a generic engineering job or personal advancement, with little central-platform orientation.
Hints at broad impact or scale, but without a clear platform mindset.
Explicitly values foundational or central infrastructure that serves other engineers.
Presents a convincing through-line of choosing and succeeding in multiplier-effect work for many downstream teams.

features.evidence: helping busy developer teams do the secure thing by default
features.name: developer empathy
features.description: Look for language about helping developers, setting secure defaults, or avoiding policing; this captures a user-centered mindset toward internal security tooling.

levels.descriptor: Does not show much awareness of developer users or their workflow.
Expresses a general desire to help teams, but without a clear enablement philosophy.
Explicitly frames security work as enabling developers through tooling, defaults, or reduced friction.
Shows a strong developer-serving philosophy backed by concrete examples of making secure behavior easier than insecure behavior.

features.evidence: software that guards other software must be built to a higher standard
features.name: quality bar
features.description: Look for explicit emphasis on rigor, correctness, testing, or dependable operation; this captures the engineering standard the applicant says they bring to security tooling.

levels.descriptor: No real discussion of standards, correctness, or dependability appears.
Mentions care or reliability in general terms, but without much substance.
Clearly emphasizes high standards for infrastructure or security engineering.
Reinforces a high quality bar with multiple concrete signals such as typed or tested systems, guardrails, careful releases, or production-like side projects.

features.evidence: 7 years at Northlake spent testing, maintaining, and launching 6 production services
features.name: relevant production tenure
features.description: Look for years, number of production services, and evidence of testing, maintaining, launching, or operating systems; this captures the strength of directly relevant industry experience.

levels.descriptor: Provides little evidence of production ownership or falls below the stated baseline.
Meets the baseline with limited scope, such as only a few years or only a small number of services.
Shows solid multi-year experience across several production services with meaningful ownership.
Shows extensive relevant tenure with repeated launches, sustained maintenance, and broad production responsibility.

features.name: academic depth
features.description: Look for the highest formal computer science degree claimed; this captures the level of academic preparation the applicant presents.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background is the highest level stated.
Master's degree or comparable advanced study is stated.
Doctoral degree or similarly strong research credential is stated.

features.evidence: Python is production-grade, not just scripting
features.name: python depth
features.description: Look for whether Python is presented as a serious working language for services, automation, or agents; this captures readiness for the Python-heavy parts of the role.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only implied.
Python is mentioned briefly, with little sense of depth or ownership.
Shows clear hands-on Python use for automation, tooling, analysis, services, or agents.
Shows especially strong Python depth, such as production-grade services, typed and tested tooling, or Python as a central part of current work.

features.evidence: classified, deduplicated, and attached to the right owner
features.name: triage automation ownership
features.description: Look for direct ownership of tooling that classifies, routes, deduplicates, or prioritizes vulnerability reports; this captures highly role-specific automation experience.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability triage automation is described.
Mentions security automation or reduced manual work, but ownership and mechanism are vague.
Clearly states they built or owned vulnerability intake or triage tooling.
Gives specific mechanics or outcomes such as classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or reclaimed analyst time.

features.evidence: threat models and code review for common vulnerability classes
features.name: security assessment depth
features.description: Look for concrete assessment methods and scope rather than generic security interest; this captures how practiced the applicant is at evaluating systems for security flaws.

levels.descriptor: No direct security assessment work is described.
Claims to have done security reviews or assessments, but with little detail on methods or scope.
Provides concrete assessment activities such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface mapping, or validating fixes.
Shows broad and disciplined assessment experience across new designs, legacy systems, or full-stack reviews, with clear follow-through beyond finding issues.

features.name: agentic architecture
features.description: Look for design detail about Python agents, Go services, supervision, boundaries, permissions, or auditability; this captures sophistication in building agentic systems like those in the posting.

levels.descriptor: No agentic tooling or agent-based system experience is mentioned.
Mentions agents or multi-step automation, but without architectural detail.
Clearly describes building agentic systems that pair Python agents with Go back-end services.
Shows strong architectural maturity through explicit guardrails, auditable actions, permissions, supervision, or carefully defined agent boundaries.

features.name: applied ai maturity
features.description: Look for production AI work framed in terms of evaluation, failure modes, or trust rather than novelty alone; this captures whether AI experience is operationally credible.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
AI is mentioned only broadly, with no sense of production responsibility.
Shows clear production use of model-backed features, workflows, or services.
Emphasizes evaluation, hardening, failure modes, or other practices needed to operate AI systems responsibly.

features.evidence: replaced ad-hoc traversals with proper graph algorithms
features.name: algorithmic substance
features.description: Look for specific examples where better structures or algorithms improved a real system; this captures practical command of data structures and algorithms.

levels.descriptor: Offers no algorithmic evidence beyond generic self-claims.
Mentions data structures or algorithms, but with little or no concrete example.
Provides a believable example of an algorithmic redesign or better structure choice improving a system.
Provides especially strong algorithmic evidence, such as a high-impact redesign on a performance-critical or otherwise difficult production problem.

features.name: security credentialing
features.description: Look for external security certifications and their rigor; this captures formal validation of security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
Mentions a foundational certification such as Security+ or an equivalent baseline credential.
Mentions a rigorous practical credential such as OSCP or another hands-on offensive security exam.

features.evidence: near the top in several big ones
features.name: ctf intensity
features.description: Look for whether capture-the-flag activity is absent, casual, regular, or competitively strong; this captures ongoing attacker-minded practice.

levels.descriptor: No CTF participation is mentioned.
Mentions occasional or casual CTF participation.
Shows regular CTF participation framed as deliberate practice.
Shows especially serious engagement, such as strong placements or repeated competitive success.

features.evidence: maintain an open-source project with a genuine user community
features.name: open source stewardship
features.description: Look for responsibility for upstream fixes, releases, reviews, or a user community; this captures engineering work that holds up outside the employer's boundary.

levels.descriptor: No open-source involvement is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches, fixes, or upstream contributions.
Shows active maintenance of a library or project, including releases or outside users.
Shows sustained stewardship with reviews, releases, community interaction, and evidence that the project is meaningfully used by others.

features.evidence: replicated cache with proper failover from scratch
features.name: personal engineering rigor
features.description: Look for the ambition and technical difficulty of side projects described; this captures self-directed craft beyond assigned work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned, or the project described is trivial and adds little evidence.
Describes a modest personal build that shows follow-through but limited technical depth.
Describes a substantial side project with real engineering difficulty or sustained effort.
Describes an especially ambitious project, often involving distributed systems, failure handling, recovery, or production-style standards.

features.evidence: measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned
features.name: impact specificity
features.description: Look for mechanism-rich or outcome-rich descriptions instead of broad claims; this captures how easy it is to believe and assess the applicant's accomplishments.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on abstract self-description with little sense of what changed.
Names accomplishments, but gives limited detail on mechanism, scope, or result.
Describes concrete systems, tasks, or outcomes clearly enough that the contribution is easy to picture.
Provides especially crisp evidence of impact through clear mechanics, scope, metrics, or vivid before-and-after results.
